rationale: The harness is submitted as the draft file exp_explicit_transfer_cost_test.go itself rather than as inline content, which is what the previous submission's files map was rejected for; the code, cases, assertions and prerequisites are otherwise unchanged. The source check just recorded withdrew the entry-point receipts' disruption because that harness issues an automatic LeadershipTransfer() before every explicit call, which leaves the account claiming an election cost with no receipt that isolates it. This experiment supplies that receipt: one explicit LeadershipTransferToServer per case, never the automatic form, on a fresh four-member cluster whose named target is either a demoted non-voter or an ordinary voter, with leader state and every member's term sampled every 10 ms for five seconds. The control shows what a legal transfer costs, one leaderless sample and one term advance with the named voter installed; the trigger shows what naming an ineligible member costs instead. A local dry run of the same file recorded nil in 0 ms with the target never leading, seven leaderless samples over 471, and the maximum term rising from two to four against a control that rose by one and installed its target, which is the contrast the account needs before it can attribute any disruption to the explicit request.

scope.description: Four-member in-memory cluster per case; one explicit LeadershipTransferToServer with no automatic request; leader state and all member terms sampled every 10 ms for five seconds.
assumptions: inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat, Election and Lease 50 ms) so an election round is observable within the window.
The demoted member's own configuration view reports the non-voter role before the request is issued.
excluded: Transfers issued concurrently with the demotion or during an election.
Clusters whose only reachable member is the non-voter.

comparisons.description: A transfer that is admitted for a named member must install that member; a false witness shows the request accepted with no leader installed.
The same single-request sequence naming an ordinary voter must install that voter, which separates the request path from the target's eligibility.
If naming an ineligible member cannot install a leader, the cluster should not pay a leaderless interval for the attempt; any leaderless sample attributes the disruption to this request alone.
